data.claim: Through the safety-vs-liveness lens from distributed systems theory: a safety property asserts that 'something bad never happens' (no incorrect state is reached), while idempotency is a specific structural guarantee (f(f(x))=f(x)). An append-only log requires the safety property: corrupted replay never arises from duplicate appends. It does not require idempotency because duplicate entries are not a correctness violation if the replay engine filters them.
